title: acre-gui clips its render until the window gets input
body:
decade started `acre-gui` as its own window in the scratch pane `terminal3` while a session worked acre-8ed0f4. The document was the default `untitled` one, a 640 by 360 canvas holding one box. Two screenshots of the pane, taken with decade's `screenshot` tool, are kept in `tmp-claude/2026-11-12-decade-scratch/` in the acre checkout. That directory is not in git and lives on one machine only.

- `before-click.png` is the first frame. The render runs off the right edge of the pane. At the scale it was drawn, the canvas would need about 940 pixels, and the pane leaves about 740.
- `after-click.png` was taken after Jack clicked the pane. The canvas fits, at about 730 pixels wide, and nothing else changed in the source.

The window's height also differs between the two. The status bar holding `untitled` sits about 40 pixels higher in the second shot, and a strip of another colour shows below the window. This suggests that acre-gui drew its first frame at a size other than the one decade gave it, and drew again only when the click arrived. Nobody has checked this. The fault could be in acre-gui, in egui's handling of a resize, or in how decade sizes the window it places.

## Open

- Whether acre-gui gets a resize event when decade places it, and whether egui repaints on it.
- Whether the same thing happens when acre-gui starts outside decade.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text:
The cause is in the compositor, not in acre-gui. A trace of a run inside decade's scratch pane logged every call to `App::logic` and `App::ui`. `logic` ran every 250 to 750 ms, as `request_repaint_after` asks. `ui` ran once, for the first frame, and never again until input. eframe 0.37 calls `ui` only on winit's `RedrawRequested`, which on Wayland waits for the compositor's frame callback. While that callback is withheld, eframe runs `logic` alone (`MISSED_REDRAW_TIMEOUT` and `update_logic_only` in eframe's `src/native/run.rs` and `epi_integration.rs`). So decade sends acre-gui's window no frame callbacks after the first frame, and acre-gui's state moves on while the window shows its first frame.

The same trace showed a reload from disk and the fitted zoom reaching `App`'s state with the window unchanged. acre-gui can do nothing about this short of drawing without frame callbacks. The fix belongs in decade.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f5ffdd3d
notes.text:
This note's conclusion is wrong. decade answers frame callbacks only after it renders. It renders only while its viewer window is on screen. Jack had probably switched Hyprland to another workspace during this run. A reproduction in decade-7091e6 froze a viewer for 4 s. Frame callbacks to the panes stopped for the same 4 s. With decade on screen, acre-gui should get its callbacks.

decade-7091e6 now covers a related decade bug. A pane screenshot taken while no viewer is on screen shows a frame the app has not redrawn. That bug explains why the screenshots in this issue showed the first frame. Nobody has explained why the first frame was drawn at the wrong size. That may be a bug of its own.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text:
I read acre-gui's code at 35b117e for a first frame drawn at a provisional size and kept until input. I found none, and I did not open a window. Nothing below has been tested against a running acre-gui.

What the code does each time eframe calls `App::ui`:

- `View::show` in `view.rs` takes the pane's `rect` from `ui.available_size()` in that same call. While the canvas is fitted, `View::show` computes the zoom and origin from that `rect`. When the zoom changes, `View::show` calls `request_repaint`.
- The cached texture is redrawn when `Drawn::pane` differs from the new pane size, whether or not the 150 ms `SETTLE` has passed. The cache key holds the pane size, so a resized pane gets a new texture in the first `ui` call after the resize.
- `App::pane` copies `Shown::rect` every frame, so the menu commands zoom about the current pane.
- eframe 0.37 asks for a repaint on winit's `WindowEvent::Resized` (`repaint_asap` in `wgpu_integration.rs`, and `egui-winit` marks `Resized` as needing a repaint). So acre-gui does not need input to learn the new size.

The screenshots show the whole window at the wrong size, with the status bar 40 pixels lower in the first shot. `View`'s texture would not move the status bar, so the first frame came from a window laid out at another size.

## Candidate causes, most likely first

1. The first frame was drawn at the size acre-gui asks for in `main.rs`, 900 by 720 points via `with_inner_size`, or at the compositor's first configure, before decade gave the window its pane size. eframe would repaint on the `Resized` that follows. On Wayland that repaint waits for a frame callback, and the memory `decade-frames-only-on-screen` records that decade sends none while it is off screen. This explains both screenshots without a fault in acre-gui. I have not checked that the measured 940 pixel canvas matches a 900 point window. The screenshots' pixel scale is unknown to me.
2. decade resized the window but winit delivered no `Resized` until the click. That would be a fault in decade's configure handling or in winit. acre-gui could not see it.
3. A fault in acre-gui's layout on the first frame. I found no code that keeps a size past the frame it was measured in.

## To settle it

Run acre-gui inside decade with decade on screen the whole time, and log `ui.ctx().content_rect()` in `App::ui`, along with each `Resized` from eframe. Two outcomes are possible. If a second `ui` call at the pane's size arrives without input, candidate 1 holds and the issue can close as decade-7091e6. If no `Resized` arrives, candidate 2 holds and the fault belongs to decade.
